page_title: DESIGN:OS Studio: open and write .fig files without Figma

sources.entry: DESIGN:OS Studio - FREE desktop design studio where your own AI agent designs on .fig files and you refine on a GPU canvas. #free #design

summary.name: DESIGN:OS Studio
summary.one_liner: A free native desktop design editor written in Rust that opens, edits and saves Figma .fig files without the Figma app, with AI coding agents able to edit documents headlessly via designos-mcp.
use_cases: Open and edit a Figma .fig file without installing Figma
Let a coding agent edit a design document through MCP tools
Export design styles and variables as DTCG token files
Generate CSS, Tailwind, React or SwiftUI code from a design
Inspect a large design kit with hundreds of thousands of nodes
Headless screenshots and exports from the command line
summary.what_it_does: Studio opens a .fig file in a native window and reads and writes it natively, with pages, layers, components, variables, styles and auto layout. The canvas is drawn on the GPU with wgpu, and the Layers panel and inspector are used to edit. Dev Mode prints code for CSS, Tailwind, React, SwiftUI, UIKit, Compose, Android XML and HTML. An Agents panel runs Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity or Gemini CLI beside the document, and those agents can edit it through designos-mcp (39 tools) or the designos CLI. The page reports a 207,601-node Untitled UI PRO v8.0 kit opening across 113 pages, though this is the vendor's own claim.
notable: Reads and writes .fig files natively, with a known save issue (#834) noted for numbered lists and some instance paints
Built-in MCP server designos-mcp with 39 tools for coding agents
GPU canvas drawn with wgpu; Dev Mode code export in 8 targets
Every agent turn is one undo step, with review and revert of changes
caveats: Source-available under PolyForm Shield, not open source
Custom shader effects are kept in files but not drawn; the inspector lists them as not rendered
Known issue #834: saving a .fig drops numbered-list formatting and writes some inherited or variable-bound instance paints as fixed values
Platform list from the page includes macOS, Windows and Linux mentions; the page does not state a full platform matrix
